title: QBR Metric Taxonomy — Pocket Guide for CS
body:
Purpose:
This pocket guide is a compact reference for Customer Success (CS) and Solutions teams preparing Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) with customers that use Redwood Inference. It gives concise, unambiguous definitions, measurement notes, and a reusable KPI table format for the four operational metrics we track most often during renewals and health conversations: latency, uptime, cost-per-token, and cache hit rate.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Renewal Managers preparing QBR slides and renewal risk assessments.
- Secondary: Product managers and SREs who want consistent definitions used in CS reporting.
- Scope: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Where measurement differs by deployment type the note is included.

Metric definitions (clean, copyable):
1) Median P95 latency (ms) — "Generation latency (P95)"
   - Definition: The 95th percentile of request generation time measured from Redwood API ingress to the first byte of model output for the request. Measured in milliseconds.
   - Formula: P95 latency = 95th percentile of (response_start_ts - request_start_ts) over the measurement window.
   - Window: rolling 7-day for trend; use 28-day for QBR snapshot.
   - Measurement notes: exclude synthetic health-check requests and zero-length prompts. For streaming APIs use time-to-first-token. For multi-stage pipelines (preprocess->model->postprocess) capture full end-to-end; annotate the breakdown in the QBR appendix.

2) Uptime (percent) — "Availability (user-facing)"
   - Definition: Percentage of time the customer’s API endpoint(s) responded successfully to user requests (2xx/3xx) within the configured timeout window.
   - Formula: Uptime % = (number_of_successful_intervals / total_intervals) * 100 where intervals are 1-minute buckets by default.
   - Window: rolling 30-day, report both 30-day and 90-day in QBR.
   - Measurement notes: For Dedicated/Private customers, report both Redwood control-plane and customer instance availability if telemetry is available. Downtime due to customer-side network misconfiguration should be annotated separately and not counted as Redwood platform downtime.

3) Cost per token (USD/token) — "Unit compute cost (effective)"
   - Definition: Effective cost attributed to customer token generation over a measurement window. This is a derived figure combining billed usage with model/runtime performance characteristics and any cost adjustments (discounts, reserved capacity credits).
   - Formula (simple): cost_per_token = billed_amount_adjusted / tokens_generated
   - Suggested normalized variant for QBR: use 'normalized cost per 1k tokens' to avoid small decimals: USD per 1,000 tokens = cost_per_token * 1000.
   - Window: monthly (to align with billing).
   - Measurement notes: include caching and batching savings in the numerator adjustments (i.e., total billed after cache/batch credits). Where reserved capacity pricing applies, include amortized fixed commitment portion in the period calculation.

4) Cache hit rate (%) — "Effective cache hit rate (prefix + KV)"
   - Definition: Fraction of requests for which a cached prefix or KV lookup avoided full model forward computation.
   - Formula: cache_hit_rate % = (cached_requests / total_model_requests) * 100
   - Window: rolling 7-day and 30-day for QBR.
   - Measurement notes: separate 'prefix cache' and 'KV cache' if available. For hybrid routing where fallback models are used, count hits only when the primary model execution was avoided.

Guidelines for measurement consistency (do this every QBR):
- Use the same windows and percentile choices across quarters for a single account to avoid spurious trend changes.
- Always show both relative delta and absolute value (e.g., P95 latency 120ms, +18% QoQ).
- Annotate known anomalies (deployments, model upgrades, traffic spikes) that materially affect the window.
- For churn-risk customers, include daily resolution charts for the last 14 days in the QBR appendix.

KPI table template (copy into slide or doc):
Columns: Metric | Current | Target | QoQ delta | SLA | Notes / Action
Sample rows (three-tier example):
Metric | Current | Target | QoQ delta | SLA | Notes / Action
Generation latency (P95) | 120 ms | <= 100 ms | +18% | P95 <= 150 ms | Investigate batch sizing; enable low-latency routing for high-priority routes
Availability (30d) | 99.88% | >= 99.9% | -0.02ppt | 99.9% monthly | One kube node restart on 2026-01-14; patch scheduled
Cost per 1k tokens | $0.95 | <= $0.85 | -5% | N/A (billing-based) | Explore more aggressive quantization or dedicated capacity commit
Cache hit rate (7d) | 42% | >= 55% | +3ppt | N/A | Cache warming recommended; review prompt templating to increase prefix reuse

Action thresholds and QBR talk track cues:
- Green: metric within target and trending favorably — highlight efficiency wins and any runway to increase usage.
- Amber: metric outside target but transient or mitigatable — present 2 remediation steps, e.g., "enable prefix caching" and "apply suggested batch policy".
- Red: metric outside target and persistent — schedule technical deep dive; propose dedicated capacity or tailored model/quantization changes.

Renewal risk score (operational quick heuristic) — single-line formula to surface during QBR prep:
- Score = weighted_sum(availability_gap, latency_gap, cost_gap, cache_gap) where each gap is normalized 0..1 and weights are default [0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1].
- Example: if a customer has 99.7% availability (gap=0.2), P95 at 180ms where target is 120ms (gap normalized to 0.5), cost per 1k tokens $1.40 vs goal $0.9 (gap=0.5), cache rate 20% vs 50% (gap=0.6) then Score = 0.4*0.2 + 0.3*0.5 + 0.2*0.5 + 0.1*0.6 = 0.08 + 0.15 + 0.10 + 0.06 = 0.39 -> ~Moderate risk.
- Use score bands: <0.15 Low risk, 0.15-0.35 Moderate, >0.35 High risk. This is a heuristic to triage accounts for renewal outreach.

Operational play snippets (one-liners to include on QBR slide):
- Latency: "We recommend enabling low-latency routing for 20% of requests to protect SLAs during peak traffic."
- Uptime: "Propose weekly canary deploys and enhanced health probes for the next 60 days to reduce restart-induced blips."
- Cost: "Trial 8-bit quantization on dev environment with representative prompts to validate quality preservation before rollout."
- Cache: "Coordinate prompt templating session with SE to increase deterministic prefixes and lift cache hit rate."

Data collection checklist for CSM before the QBR (copy into calendar invite):
- [ ] Export 7d and 30d metrics (latency P95, uptime 30d, cache hit 7d) from Redwood Console.
- [ ] Pull monthly billing statement and tokens_generated from billing console (for cost per token).
- [ ] Note any model rollouts, infra upgrades, or planned maintenance during the window.
- [ ] Attach relevant Jira tickets or incident reports to the QBR appendix.

Appendix (quick reference):
- Common dashboard widgets to include: time-series P95 latency with model-change annotations; availability heatmap by region; cost-per-1k tokens trend; cache hit breakdown (prefix vs KV).
- Suggested tags for Redwood Console exports: account:<customer-name>, route:<route-id>, model:<model-id>, environment:<prod|staging>.
- Contacts: Solutions Engineering lead (Sofia Nguyen), SRE escalation (Riley Brooks), Billing ops (Omar Patel).

Notes on privacy and on-prem customers:
- For Private deployments with limited telemetry, use customer-provided logs for latency and cache hit calculations and annotate measurement method in the QBR.
- Do not include raw request payloads in QBR attachments; use aggregated metrics and redacted examples.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-10: first draft (Leah Martinez).
- 2025-12-03: added renewal risk heuristic and checklist (Sofia Nguyen).
- 2026-02-15: clarified cost-per-token amortization for reserved capacity (Omar Patel).

Quick copy checklist for slide creation (one-paragraph):
Paste KPI table (use template above), include two bullets of context (one technical, one business), then show renewal risk band and up to three proposed customer-specific actions. Keep the slide focused — no more than one dense chart; move detailed charts to the appendix.
